metadata.title: Federal Employees v. Department of Interior, 526 U.S. 86 (1999) (No. 97-1184)
metadata.creator: Supreme Court of the United States
metadata.description:
Case name: Federal Employees v. Department of Interior

Opinion filed: 1999-03-03

Docket No.: 97-1184

Citations:
• 143 L. Ed. 2d 171
• 119 S. Ct. 1003
• 526 U.S. 86
• 1999 U.S. LEXIS 1710

Case holding summaries:
• administrative agencies not estopped from changing their interpretations of a statute, but affording revised interpretations less deference
• When “the [s]tatute’s language [is] sufficiently ambiguous or open on the point,” courts must defer “to reasonable interpretation or elaboration by the agency charged with its execution.”
• defining the doctrine of in pari materia, citing several cases where the Court applied this doctrine to aid in its construction of a variety of statutes, and arguing that the doctrine was now "well established"
• “[A] single, unreviewed decision [based on an executive order that preceded the statute] does not demonstrate the kind of historical practice that one might assume would be reflected in the Statute.”
